title: Coster the Jesuit defends kneeling prayer before Christ’s image, adorning images, candles, and carrying statues in processions
source_text: XVIII. Ista enim passim in tota Ecclesia Romana fiunt, nec diserte & publice improbantur ab ullis, qui in Ecclesia illa authoritate, doctrina & dignitate eminent, ac pro Orthodoxis habentur, sed contra a multis publice probantur, atque defenduntur. Ut, exempli gratia, a Costerio Jesuita in Enchiridio Controversiarum capite de usu & veneratione imaginum. Proinde, inquit, reprehendendi non sunt Christiani qui Christum in sua imagine flexis genibus, apertis capitibus, junctis manibus adorant & precantur, ab eoque misericordiam, auxilium & opem implorant. Neque illi qui imagines vestibus, monilibus, & id genus aliis ornare solent. Nec reprehensione digna, sed commendanda est Christianorum consuetudo, qua cereos, in honorem sanctorum, coram imaginibus accendunt. Denique Ecclesiae consuetudo circumferendi statuas & imagines in supplicationibus antiquo usu comprobata est, & merito commendanda.
pass_a_gloss: For these things are done everywhere throughout the whole Roman Church, and are not expressly and publicly disapproved by any who are eminent in that Church in authority, doctrine, and dignity and are held for Orthodox, but on the contrary are publicly approved and defended by many. As, for example, by Coster the Jesuit in the Enchiridion of Controversies, in the chapter on the use and veneration of images. Therefore, he says, Christians are not to be blamed who adore and pray to Christ in His image with bent knees, uncovered heads, and joined hands, and from Him implore mercy, help, and aid. Nor those who are accustomed to adorn images with garments, necklaces, and things of that kind. Nor is the Christians’ custom blameworthy but commendable by which they light candles before images in honor of the saints. Finally the Church’s custom of carrying about statues and images in processions is approved by ancient usage and deservedly to be commended.
pass_b_english: Jesuit Coster publicly defends kneeling prayer before Christ’s image, rich adornment, saint-candles, and statue processions as commendable Church custom.
